rounds.text: Suratwwala Business Group Ltd is dramatically under-appreciated by the market, trading at an attractive P/E of 14.5x [E1] that compresses to 11x against a sector benchmark of 32.93x [E6]. This valuation disconnect is completely detached from the company's stellar financial performance, highlighted by a trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of 177% and profit growth of 195% [E17, E21]. The business generates world-class returns, boasting an ROE of 36.8% and an ROCE of 27.3% [E12, E13], alongside a 5-year median ROE of 43% [E26] that dwarfs the sector median ROCE of just 6.1% [E70]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow model places intrinsic value at Rs 68 per share against a market price of just Rs 24.6, offering a massive margin of safety of 63.8% [E43, E44], while a reverse DCF shows that the current price absurdly prices in a mere 4.0% earnings growth [E45]. Fundamental strength is starkly outpacing stock sentiment, evidenced by profit growth exceeding 5-year price growth and beating 1-year price growth by 236% [E54, E55], creating a classic turnaround opportunity where results score 90 out of 100 while the price remains heavily suppressed [E66]. Conceded: the stock sits 23% of the way up its 52-week range and is currently trading below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with an RS rating of 0 [E5, E48, E49].

Despite reported short-term profit growth, Suratwwala Business Group Ltd exhibits severe cash generation and working capital disconnects, highlighted by a cash conversion ratio of -0.00x where operating cash flow sits at Rs -0 Cr and free cash flow drops to Rs -6 Cr in Mar 2026 [E33, E35]. This alarming divergence between paper profits and actual cash realization is compounded by an explicit warning flag that the company might be capitalizing its interest costs [E58]. Compounded share price growth over 1 year has cratered by -41% [E24], and the stock languishes well below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with a relative-strength rating of 0 against the Nifty 500 [E48, E49]. Operating margins have also deteriorated, contracting by 3 percentage points over three years to 45% in Mar 2026 alongside an inconsistent yearly margin trend [E29, E31]. Furthermore, borrowings have expanded to Rs 76 Cr in Mar 2026 from Rs 60 Cr a year earlier, increasing financial leverage while cash flows remain deeply negative [E38]. Conceded: [E19, E25, E43].

Conceded: the bull correctly notes that the company posts high trailing sales and profit growth, an ROE of 36.8%, and an ROCE of 27.3% [E12, E13, E17, E21], but these glowing figures completely mask a catastrophic disconnect where reported profits are not translating into actual cash [E33]. Specifically, the cash conversion for Mar 2026 sits at -0.00x because operating cash flow was negative at Rs -0 Cr, with operating cash flow making up a meager 32% of operating profit [E33, E34, E36], pointing directly to severe risks around uncollected receivables or aggressive accruals [E33]. Compounding this alarming cash drain, free cash flow plunged to Rs -6 Cr and total borrowings increased from Rs 60 Cr to Rs 76 Cr [E35, E38], while Screener explicitly flags that the company might be capitalizing its interest costs [E58]. The bull's cheap valuation multiples and high intrinsic value models ignore that operating margins have eroded across yearly and quarterly metrics with an inconsistent trend [E29, E30, E31, E32], and that the stock suffers from a zero relative-strength rating, a brutal 43.1% twelve-month decline, and massive annualized volatility of 62.1% [E49, E50, E52].
